# apple_user_visible_app (Resource)

Gives a team member access to one app. Each resource manages one app, so several configurations can grant their own apps to the same user. The user needs `all_apps_visible = false`, and must have accepted their invitation: until then, applying fails and the next apply after they accept succeeds. Destroying it removes access to this app only. Import it with `<user email or ID>/<app_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Applies once dev@example.com has accepted their invitation.
resource "apple_user_visible_app" "dev_example" {
  user_email = apple_user.dev.email
  app_id     = data.apple_app.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the app.
- `user_email` (String) Email address of the user, e.g. `apple_user.dev.email`.

### Read-Only

- `user_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the user.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = apple_user_visible_app.dev_example
  identity = {
    user_id = "6a5b4c3d-2e1f-4a0b-9c8d-7e6f5a4b3c2d"
    app_id  = "1234567890"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `app_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the app.
- `user_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the user.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <user email or ID>/<app_id>
terraform import apple_user_visible_app.dev_example dev@example.com/1234567890
```
